fluff.overview:
The Neanderthal is a Regulan-designed assault BattleMech produced by Tactical Advantage, LLC on Regulus. First entering service in 3124 with the NTL-UG model and refined into the NTL-AG configuration by 3128, the design was conceived as a lighter alternative to the Lyran Commonwealth's fearsome one-hundred-ton Berserker. Rather than simply scaling down the heavier brawler, Tactical Advantage re-envisioned the close-combat concept with typical Regulan flair, producing a distinctive eighty-ton machine built around aggressive melee doctrine.

The Neanderthal's blocky, imposing silhouette has become a symbol of Regulan martial prowess, and its reputation for devastating hand-to-hand combat has made it a feared presence on battlefields across the Free Worlds League region.
fluff.capabilities:
The Neanderthal's combat philosophy centers on closing to melee distance as quickly as possible and overwhelming opponents with raw physical violence. Powered by a massive LTV 400 extra-light fusion engine, the 'Mech achieves a respectable 86 km/h under normal conditions. The incorporation of Triple Strength Myomer pushes this to nearly 100 km/h when the 'Mech runs hot, simultaneously amplifying the devastating force of its right-hand hatchet. This combination makes the Neanderthal exceptionally dangerous once it reaches striking distance.

A Guardian ECM Suite integrated with the Garret C22A communications system complicates enemy targeting solutions, buying the Neanderthal precious seconds to close the gap. The specific weapons loadout varies between configurations, but each emphasizes firepower suited to the closing approach followed by brutal melee engagement.

Unlike the Berserker it was inspired by, the Neanderthal avoids MASC in favor of TSM, trading instant acceleration for sustained reliability. While this eliminates the explosive burst speed of the Lyran design, it removes the risk of catastrophic actuator failure entirely. Durallex Super Medium ferro-fibrous armor provides solid protection for the assault approach, though concentrated fire from multiple opponents remains a serious threat before the 'Mech reaches close-combat range.
fluff.history:
The Neanderthal's development grew from the Regulan Fiefs' desire to field a homegrown close-combat BattleMech capable of matching the fearsome reputation of the Lyran Berserker. Tactical Advantage, LLC took on the challenge, and rather than attempting a direct copy of the one-hundred-ton Lyran design, the Regulan manufacturer crafted an original eighty-ton platform that re-envisioned the concept with distinctly Regulan engineering sensibilities.

The initial NTL-UG model entered production in 3124 and quickly demonstrated the chassis's potential, though its laser-heavy armament was seen as a mismatch for the design's close-combat strengths. By 3128, the refined NTL-AG replaced the UG as the primary production model, embracing the Neanderthal's melee doctrine with weapons better suited to close-quarters engagements.

The Neanderthal saw significant action during the Dark Age, with the Twenty-first Regulan Hussars putting the design through its paces in 3130 when the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth's Twenty-fifth Marik Militia landed on Wallis. The Regulans intercepted the raiding force, and the Hussars' Neanderthals played a crucial role in the engagement. Expecting the older NTL-UG, the raiders attempted to keep the Regulans at range rather than allowing them to reach melee distance. The Twenty-first concentrated on closing the gap as rapidly as possible, triggering their TSM systems and engaging in devastating physical combat that caught the enemy by surprise.

Although the Twenty-fifth largely escaped Wallis with significant materiel stockpiles from Ronin, Inc., the damage inflicted by the Hussars' Neanderthals nearly negated the raid's gains. Of two lances deployed in defense, only three Neanderthals remained combat-worthy when the raiders withdrew. The fierce defense established the Neanderthal's reputation as a serious close-combat threat, and few raiders have since underestimated the design. The distinctive appearance of a Neanderthal on the battlefield tends to prompt slower units to pull back, while faster elements concentrate fire in an effort to cripple the 'Mech before it reaches striking distance.

The Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, drawn by the Berserker's heritage and the Neanderthal's similar combat philosophy, arranged purchases through the Army Supply Corps for deployment along the Free Worlds League border. This Lyran interest, combined with sales to various mercenary commands operating in the region, has given the Neanderthal a broader operational footprint than most Regulan designs typically achieve.
fluff.deployment: This variant was the original production variant of the Neanderthal, entering service in 3124. Armed with a large pulse laser and pairs of large and small lasers, the UG relied more heavily on ranged energy weapons than its successor. This overreliance on standoff weaponry proved a poor match for the Neanderthal's melee-oriented chassis design, as the laser array encouraged pilots to maintain distance rather than close to hatchet range where TSM-enhanced strength could be fully exploited. Mounting only ten double heat sinks compounded this issue, as the laser complement generated considerable waste heat that limited sustained fire. These shortcomings led directly to the development of the AG model, though the UG continues to see active service.
